name: DoodleMath
line: DoodleMath reviews in Power Ups about every 20 days. In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice.
description: AMP vs DoodleMath: DoodleMath teaches by topic and reviews in Power Ups. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: DoodleMath's algorithm builds a work plan from a child's answers, opens each new topic with an explanation, and returns to weak areas in a Power Up about every 20 days [6][7][8]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer, and learned skills come back in ordinary practice.

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. In DoodleMath, review comes in Power Ups: 15-question sets on areas its algorithm flags for support, usually about once every 20 days [8]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [15].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step and never the answer, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In DoodleMath the teaching comes with the topic. A new topic opens with an interactive explanation in three parts, a hint sits behind a question-mark button, and a Help button reopens the explanation [7]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [16].

reasons.title: What counts as learned
reasons.body: In AMP an answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. DoodleMath counts progress in stars and a DoodleAge [9]. We found no rule for when a skill counts as learned in the pages we read [6][9].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math and runs from counting through precalculus in one program, on one map of skills. A learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels. DoodleMath covers kindergarten through grade 5 [1][2].

rows.range: Kindergarten through grade 5, aligned to Common Core [1][2].
rows.start: No separate placement test described. Its algorithm, Proxima, learns from each answer and adjusts the work plan [6].
rows.teaching: At the topic. A new topic opens with an interactive explanation: a recap, short steps, then applying it. Hints on request [7].
rows.next: Proxima's work plan for each child. Parents can also set work in any topic [4][6].
rows.mastery: Progress is counted in stars and a DoodleAge [9]. No rule for when a skill is learned found in the pages we read [6][9].
rows.review: Power Ups: 15-question sets on areas its algorithm flags for support, usually about once every 20 days [8].
rows.print: None found in the pages we read [1][6].
rows.adult: By Doodle's account, parents do not need to set or mark work. They can set work in any topic [4].
rows.reports: A Parent Dashboard, and an online hub that tracks progress [4][6].
rows.evidence: Two summer studies of its own, with no sample sizes published [3]. No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [13][14].

theirs: DoodleMath, spelled DoodleMaths in the UK, is an app from DoodleLearning. In the U.S. it covers kindergarten through grade 5 and is aligned to Common Core [1]. By Doodle's account, home educators use it alongside their own curriculum [4].

Doodle's algorithm, Proxima, learns from each answered question and builds each child's work plan [6]. A new topic opens with an interactive explanation in three parts: a recap, a series of short steps, and a chance to apply it, with tools such as number lines, place-value counters and a fraction builder [7]. Questions come in many forms, including typed answers, fractions, number lines and multiple choice [10]. Children earn DoodleStars and keep a daily streak [11]. About once every 20 days, a 15-question Power Up returns to areas Proxima flags for support [8].
credit: Interactive explanations with number lines, place-value counters and a fraction builder [7].
It adjusts each child's work plan from every answer [6].
Questions and explanations can be read aloud [5].

theirs: DoodleLearning's impact page describes two summer studies of its own with 10-year-olds [3]. In the first, children chose how much to use the app, and results were compared by level of use. In the second, children were randomly given access to the app or not. The page gives no sample sizes, effect sizes, authors or dates, and the full report sits behind a form [3][12].

A Doodle help page credits a University of Bath study with this figure: children earning 15 stars a day gained about 1.94 years in 12 months, against 0.84 for non-users [9]. It is measured in Doodle's own units, and the page gives no sample, authors or date [9].

Doodle states that DoodleMath meets ESSA Tier IV, the tier for a published rationale [3]. DoodleMath has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [13][14]. We found no independent outcome study on Doodle's site.
ours: The two findings that bear most on this comparison: mixed, spaced practice scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks on the researchers' own test a month later, in a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [15], and worked examples improve math performance, with an average effect of g = 0.48 across 55 studies [16]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want each new topic introduced with an interactive explanation and on-screen tools such as number lines.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate test.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in ordinary practice, mixed with other math.
You want a hint and a lesson at every problem, and the worked steps after every answer.
You want a skill to count only when it is right without help, more than once.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math, or ready for math past grade 5.

questions.question: How is AMP different from DoodleMath?
questions.answer: DoodleMath builds a work plan from a child's answers, opens each new topic with an explanation, and returns to weak areas in a Power Up about every 20 days [6][7][8]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does DoodleMath work?
questions.answer: DoodleLearning describes two summer studies of its own, with no sample sizes or effect sizes published [3]. DoodleMath has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse, and we found no independent outcome study [13][14].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
